subject: SENTINEL: MAP + evaluation cadence & canary runbook (post-signature)
summary: Post-signature mutual action plan with embedded evaluation gates, canary criteria, migration windows, and training milestones for Sentinel Health. Includes ops runbook and ask list for procurement and solutions ops.

Subject: SENTINEL: MAP + evaluation cadence & canary runbook (post-signature)

Amelia —

Congrats again on the signature. Attached is a working draft of the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation plan we discussed: rollout milestones, canary gating criteria, migration windows, and the training cadence for your three pilot sites. Key highlights up front: 

- Week 1 (Mar 27–Apr 2): Provisioning & baseline tests (non-prod).
- Week 2 (Apr 3–Apr 9): Canary cohort #1 (10% traffic, 1 region) with defined KPIs and automatic rollback thresholds.
- Weeks 3–5 (Apr 10–Apr 30): Progressive rollout to pilot sites with weekly eval checkpoints.
- Training: two live training sessions (admin + engineering) during Week 2 and on-call handoff in Week 4.

I attached a short EvalPlan (EvalPlan_Sentinel_v2.pdf) that lists the prompt-level test sets, latency and correctness thresholds, and the data retention/audit expectations for your compliance team. Please review the canary gating thresholds on page 3 — the idea is to automate an immediate fallback to the region fallback model if token latency or error rate exceed our SLOs.

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Confirm the pilot site list (we used Westlake, Northgate, and Harborview).
2) Confirm the target admin + infra attendees for the training sessions (see proposed dates in the MAP sheet).
3) Procurement: please share the preferred PO cadence or DocuSign link for the reserved capacity agreement.

I’m looping in Monica and Vivek from our delivery team to confirm runbook items and finalize the canary checklist. Marcus — if procurement will use a signing tool, let us know and we’ll push the acceptance docs.

Thanks — we’ll plan a 30-minute sync next Tuesday to lock dates if that works.

—Aditya

Aditya / team —

Quick ops notes after a pass through the MAP sheet and the canary checklist: 

- Automated rollback: we can host the initial canary in Redwood Hosted (us-west-2) and configure automated routing fallback by policy. That means 0 manual steps on Sentinel's side for the rollback itself. We will, however, require an on-call contact and an approval cadence for any extended rollback (>30 minutes).
- Canary criteria we propose: 95th percentile token latency < 220ms, error rate < 0.6% over a rolling 5-minute window, per-prompt correctness above 92% on the eval set. These are slightly tighter than the sheet — suggesting conservative defaults for the first two cohorts.
- Migration windows: recommend low-traffic windows: Sat 0200–0500 local for Harborview, Sun 0100–0400 for Westlake. If Northgate is approved, add Wed 0100–0400.

A) Vivek: prepare the Hosted provisioning playbook and confirm infra lead (who will be the on-call during Week 2).

Amelia / team —

I populated the smoke-test harness in the EvalPlan (see page 2 of EvalPlan_Sentinel_v2.pdf). Quick notes on gating: 

- Canary fidelity checks run every 5 minutes. If any of the following happen, the system triggers a soft-fail (alerts ops and pauses new canary traffic): 95th pctl latency > 220ms OR 5-min error rate > 0.6%.
- If soft-fail persists for 10 minutes, an automated rollback to fallback model is executed and a P1 ticket is opened with both parties on escalation.
- For clinical correctness checks we run a daily prompt diff against the held eval set; any regression >2% triggers a manual halt and immediate joint review.

I'll add the CLI validation steps Vivek mentioned and a brief recorded training snippet for the admin workflow into the Drive folder.

Regards,
